hero.role: I help you find the words when it's hard to say what's on your mind in your relationships — in a way that brings you closer, not further apart.

quoteBlock.quote: “Communication became especially important to me because, as a child, I experienced firsthand what it costs when two people can no longer truly talk to each other.”
quoteBlock.leadIn: This is where my path toward coaching began — and today I do this work so that others don't have to go through the same thing, whether from the adult's or the child's side.

about.heading: About me
about.introParagraph1: What is my own inner motivation? For a long time I didn't know who I was, what my values were — if I even had any — or who I wanted to become. I started my own journey of self-discovery at 28, because I needed a drastic change. I got divorced and had to figure out what to do with my life and myself. So the process didn't begin with conscious self-development — I was simply at a point in my life where I'd hit rock bottom and had to rebuild myself. There were difficult moments, hard days, hours spent crying through — but I want to tell you this: I'm here, if you feel like you've been left alone with your thoughts. I listen with real attention, and I support you in finding your own path.
about.pathParagraph: I always loved talking with people and listening to them. More than that — I felt that people opened up to me easily. While searching for my own way forward, I became certain that I wanted to learn more about social relationships. So I enrolled at the University of Szeged and earned a degree in Social Pedagogy. In the meantime, in my new relationship, I also received the dream I had longed for so much — I became a mother, which comes with its own set of challenges. As a career-changing mother, after several years away from work, I needed to adapt to new expectations in the workplace, so I completed a career-coaching course. I founded my own business, and then wanted to broaden my knowledge further, so I also took part in a Family and Couples Coaching course. Crowning all of this, I completed a Thomas Gordon communication training to further develop my personal effectiveness.
about.reflectionParagraph1: After a long process, I can say today that I'm a balanced person, living in a balanced marriage and a happy motherhood. That doesn't mean there are no rough patches, that we never clash over our own interests, or that I never lose my patience with my child — but we try to channel all of that into something healthy and sustainable for everyone involved. Over the past few years I've had to hold my own in many different roles, and the experience from them has taught me not just as a private person, but has also let me reflect as a professional on the difficulties that come up.
about.reflectionParagraph2: My goal is to pass on my knowledge and motivation, because I firmly believe there is hope even for our fraying human relationships. I think this rests on two pillars: communication and determination. I first heard the term "empowerment" at university — to me, it means supporting a person in recognizing and mobilizing their own resources, so they become able to shape their own path. That's exactly why I created the "Mothers for each other · Women for ourselves" community too.
about.reflectionParagraph3: Feel free to reach out if you feel stuck in your life, if something feels off but you're not sure which way to turn. I'd love to welcome you to our free introductory conversation.

services.heading: How can I help you?
services.intro: Three areas, three life situations — see which one you recognize yourself in.

partnership.title: Relationship coaching
partnership.situation: When it's already hard to hear each other, and conversations tend to pull you apart rather than bring you together.
partnership.blockquote: If you'd finally like to say what's on your mind in a way that brings you closer instead of further apart — let's work on it together.

communication.title: Assertive communication
communication.situation: When you want to say what's on your mind — in a way that preserves the relationship too. "How do I say it?"
chips: I want to set a boundary
I want to say what hurts me
I don't want conflict, but I don't want to stay silent either
I'm always the one who adapts
It's hard for me to stand up for myself
I want to be honest without hurting the other person

parenting.title: Parental communication and family atmosphere
parenting.situation: When you want to show up differently at home. This is for you if the following sound familiar:
chips: "How do I set boundaries without punishment?"
"How do I say no without it turning into a fight?"
"My partner and I don't agree on parenting either."
"What atmosphere are we creating at home?"

community.kicker: Mothers for each other · Women for ourselves
community.heading: Be part of a judgment-free, connection-rich, supportive community.
community.body: Supporting. Connecting. Speaking honestly. A place where you don't have to carry the load alone — where other mothers and women understand what you're going through, and where you can share your thoughts in a safe space.
